source.stem: A plane mirror lies at x=25 cm and a stationary bead at x=5 cm. The mirror moves to x=28 cm while the bead stays fixed. Determine the initial and final image coordinates, then explain which symmetry forces the result.
source.decisive_work: Locate the virtual image in one fixed coordinate frame and defend the mirror-symmetry rule.

shortest_valid_route: Fix one laboratory coordinate and define mirror plane m and object position x_o
Use reflection symmetry to obtain x_i=2m−x_o
Evaluate both positions, image displacement and object–image separation independently
Test rigid co-translation as an invariant
task.protected_decisive_work: Combine changes of mirror and object in a fixed coordinate frame, distinguishing image motion from object–image separation.
task.model_conditions: Ideal plane mirror, one-dimensional perpendicular positions measured in one fixed laboratory axis, rays approximated geometrically.

concept_model_selection.evidence: Choosing a fixed-axis mirror symmetry model rather than a moving-object shortcut is decisive

representation_translation.evidence: Two frames (before and after) need explicit signed coordinates

reasoning_chain_length.evidence: Two transformations are linked: obtain image position and compare object–image separation

algebra_computational_load.evidence: Integer arithmetic only, after model selection

trap_exception_sensitivity.evidence: A memorized 'twice the mirror motion' law fails when the object also moves
